title: Linux - Processes, Crontab, Systemd, D-Bus (formerly Processes, Crontab, Systemd, D-Bus)
html:
Processes, Crontab, Systemd, and D-Bus

Scheduled jobs and interprocess communication can launch code with privileges different from those of the caller. Inspect the owner, command, and writable inputs of a service or job before testing it.

  • Process enumeration and service paths covers process trees, runtime files, and systemd execution chains.
  • Cron jobs and systemd timers covers scheduled-task discovery and writable inputs.
  • D-Bus enumeration and command injection privilege escalation covers the message bus and privileged service methods.
  • Payloads to execute collects payloads that can be used when an execution path has been identified.

For a wider review of cron jobs and systemd services, use the Linux privilege escalation checklist.
